walkthroughs.body_html:
Formation of Planetary Systems — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Formation of Planetary Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Formation of Planetary Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why do astronomers infer the existence of dark matter?
options: Because the universe looks dark at night.
Light from the most distant galaxies.
Dark matter has been directly observed in telescopes.
Visible matter alone cannot account for galaxy rotation curves and gravitational lensing.

mcqs.q: What is a black hole's event horizon?
options: The boundary beyond which not even light can escape.
A literal horizon you can walk to.
Light from the most distant galaxies.
The visible 'edge' of the black hole.

mcqs.q: What is the cosmic microwave background?
options: Background noise from human microwave ovens.
Relic radiation from when the universe became transparent, about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
Because the universe looks dark at night.
Light from the most distant galaxies.
